note: Seen wearing the belt as late as 30 November 1997 (msg_id M2pF_iBHhmkJ, cited not served); a second, unreconciled claimant to this title is billed in a BWA card this collection DOES serve (promotions/bwa/archive/bwa-raw-footage-1997-09-11.html), placing a different wrestler's win in September 1997 -- both readings are carried, per the no-auto-merge rule, neither resolved.

title: iewf-lwc-rio-grande
label: "Armitage" Steve Spector
how: Won the title with a pair of wins, first over Stephen Lords and Tony Ruiz and then over Ryan Decker "to attain the actual belt", as Aaron Wexler recounts on the broadcast of 15 November 1998.
note: Retained the title over Adam Craig in a two out of three falls match at Last Tangle In Texarkana on 15 November 1998, and is billed to defend it against Thantasia, the winner of that night's battle royal, on 20 December 1998 in Longview. No held document records that match; the next holder on file, Thantasia, has no won date beyond 'after 6 December 1998', and Spector's reign has no end date.

title: iewf-lwc-rio-grande
label: Thantasia

won.source: /promotions/iewf-lwc/archive/lwc-stampede-dec-6-1998-12-10.html: "Thantasia vs. Steve Spector [c]". The broadcast of 6 December 1998 prints the title match for 20 December with Spector still the champion; no held document dates Thantasia's win.

note: No won-date survives; the title was already held entering the held record's newly-found 1999 documents.

title: iewf-lwc-silver-city
label: "America's Perfection" Alex Wallace

won.source: /promotions/iewf-lwc/archive/lwc-stampede-oct-25-1998-10-27.html: "two-time and REIGNING Silver City Champion"; /promotions/iewf-lwc/archive/lwc-stampede-nov-1-1998-11-03.html: "Alex Wallace (4-1) [c] vs. Big Bad Boris (8-5)". No held document dates the win; the broadcast of 1 November 1998 has him retain the title in a dark match.

lost.source: /promotions/iewf-lwc/archive/lwc-last-tangle-in-texarkana-1998-11-22.html: "by way of a pinfall, and NEW Silver City Champion"

note: The first of his two reigns is dated nowhere in the held documents and has no row. At Last Tangle In Texarkana Jennifer Dial declared the title vacant for him while announcing his retirement, but he took the belt back in the ring, refused to retire and defended it in the four corners main event, where Tex Violence pinned him to win it.

title: iewf-lwc-twin-pistol
label: The Nine Inch Males

won.source: /promotions/iewf-lwc/archive/lwc-last-tangle-in-texarkana-1998-11-22.html: "since they won them back on July 19th in the Pinfall Bunkhouse Battle Royal"

note: Won in the Pinfall Bunkhouse Battle Royal of 19 July 1998 and kept through the Sunday Stampede of 1 November 1998 and Last Tangle In Texarkana on 15 November 1998, where the champions' match ended when B. Lackey made Mark Wugger submit and the pair kept the belts. Retained against Black Sun Rising at a three-day interfederation pay-per-view in April 1999.

title: iewf-lwc-six-gun
label: Mark Cutter

won.source: /promotions/iewf-lwc/archive/lwc-last-tangle-in-texarkana-1998-11-22.html: "Mark Cutter was the one he won it from". The card printed in the Sunday Stampede of 4 October 1998 already bills him as the champion ('Mark Cutter [c] vs. Mark Wugger'); no held document dates the win.

lost.source: /promotions/iewf-lwc/archive/lwc-stampede-oct-4-1998-10-13.html: "Mark Cutter [c] vs. Mark Wugger"; /promotions/iewf-lwc/archive/lwc-stampede-oct-18-1998-10-19.html: "the new LWC Six Gun Champ, one half of Bigger Than Hollywood, Mark Wugger". No document of 11 October, the date of the card that bills the match, is held.

note: A video package shown on the Last Tangle In Texarkana broadcast has him winning the title; no held document dates that win.

title: iewf-lwc-silver-city
label: Tex Violence

won.source: /promotions/iewf-lwc/archive/lwc-last-tangle-in-texarkana-1998-11-22.html: "by way of a pinfall, and NEW Silver City Champion"

note: Defended and retained the title against a challenger on the promotion's 14 February 1999 broadcast.
how: Pinned Alex Wallace with a flying guillotine legdrop across the steel railing in the four corners match against Wallace, Robert Donovan and Midori-iro Kikai at Last Tangle In Texarkana, thirty-nine minutes and fifty seconds in.

title: iewf-lwc-rio-grande
label: "Psycho" Johnny Rage
note: Won a Heaven and Hell match after his fallen opponent unexpectedly stirred to make the winning pinfall.

title: iewf-lwc-six-gun
label: "Bullywug" Glenn Hudson

won.source: /promotions/iewf-lwc/archive/lwc-stampede-oct-4-1998-10-13.html: "Mark Cutter [c] vs. Mark Wugger"; /promotions/iewf-lwc/archive/lwc-stampede-oct-18-1998-10-19.html: "the new LWC Six Gun Champ, one half of Bigger Than Hollywood, Mark Wugger". The broadcast of 15 November 1998 adds that he won it from Mark Cutter; no document of 11 October, the date of the card that bills the match, is held.

lost.source: /promotions/iewf-lwc/archive/lwc-last-tangle-in-texarkana-1998-11-22.html: "due to the fact that B. Lackey forced Mark Wugger to submit, he is the new Six Gun Champion"

note: Billed as Mark Wugger. Lost the title at Last Tangle In Texarkana in the Twin Pistol match, when his partner B. Lackey, Rob James, forced him to submit with an ankle lock after B. Astard turned on Mark Cutter. A video package shown on every broadcast also has him winning the title from Casey James with No Hard Feelings, in an earlier reign no held document dates.

title: iewf-lwc-six-gun
label: Rob James

won.source: /promotions/iewf-lwc/archive/lwc-last-tangle-in-texarkana-1998-11-22.html: "due to the fact that B. Lackey forced Mark Wugger to submit, he is the new Six Gun Champion"

note: Retained by forfeit on 6 December 1998 when Mark Cutter did not appear for a challenge match. Billed as champion at the April 1999 interfederation pay-per-view, where he defended the Twin Pistol Championships instead.
how: Forced his tag partner Glenn Hudson, the reigning champion, to submit with an ankle lock in the Twin Pistol match against Bigger Than Hollywood at Last Tangle In Texarkana, after B. Astard turned on Mark Cutter.
